title: Packaging and back-end lithography: steppers, digital/maskless and panel-level lithography for advanced packaging (Canon, Nikon, ASML XT:260, others)
why_it_matters: Canon reports a large rise in back-end lithography sales on AI packaging demand, ASML shipped its first packaging scanner and Nikon is betting on digital back-end lithography; this segment sits outside the front-end lithography figures.
questions: What are unit sales and revenue of packaging lithography tools by vendor and technology?
Which packaging steps (RDL, interposer, panel-level) use which lithography tools?
How concentrated is the supply and who are the non-Japanese/Dutch suppliers?
primary_sources: Canon annual report and results presentations

title: EUV sub-tier supply network beyond Zeiss and TRUMPF: tin-droplet generators, collectors, multilayer coatings, vacuum and mechatronics modules (VDL-ETG, Prodrive) and their single-source status
why_it_matters: ASML says EUV parts are often single-sourced ('single sourcing, dual competence') and relies on ~900 product suppliers; ZEISS SMT cites a 1,200-partner network; only Zeiss is named as sole source publicly.
questions: Which EUV modules have a single supplier and where are they located?
What did ASML disclose about supplier capacity constraints in 2022-2026?
How do VDL, Prodrive and other Brainport suppliers depend on ASML revenue?
